description: Path A test for the borromean-quark energy-scale ansatz: compares the counit net difference ε(ΔNF)=h²/2−h against the Markov-trace difference tr_M(ΔNF) of the nucleon single-wrap NF, symbolically exact. Determines whether the per-braid mass tower reproduces the unweighted net at leading order (ansatz derivable) or differs by the Markov weight z (ansatz is a counit structural choice). Derive-or-refute; nothing wired.

data.verdict: CROSS-CHECK CONFIRMS prop:qbeta-counit-closed-form (already Lean-proved): Δtr_M/Δnet → 1/2 = z (Markov weight at q→1). Computed here via the Wedderburn Σ_λ y_λ χ^λ route (vs the corpus prop's direct NF-weight route) — agrees. The counit ε (net) and Markov trace tr_M are DERIVED-distinct functionals: tr_M(β)=⟨β,1⟩ (loop/mass), ε(β)=⟨β,ω⟩, ω=G⁻¹1 (transition/decay) per prop:qbeta-counit-transition; β-decay is a transition ⇒ counit. This ratio→z IS the corpus's 'trace falls short by a factor of two'. NOT a novel refutation: the functional selection is derived; the sole open item is the non-perturbative tower convergence conj:qbeta-trace-counit-convergence. This probe is one N=0 boundary data point for it.
